In summary, our research is concerned with
how eye movements are used in the construction of mental imagery and the role of eye movement patterns in memory retrieval.
the relationship between eye movement, mental imagery and episodic memory retrieval.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
eye movements play an active and facilitory role during mental imagery and retrieval of visual memories.
the eye movements produced during mental imagery and during memory retrieval have a functional role, and that this role is related to the content of the mental imagery and the memory to be retrieved.
eye movements are a necessary component of the mental processes that underlie memory retrieval and mental imagery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the eye movements during mental visualisation are not simply the result of a motoric reproduction of the encoding phase.
eye movements during mental image generation reflect content and spatial structure.

eye movements during mental image generation are not a simple reproduction of eye movements during the encoding of the same scene but rather a complex interaction between the memory trace of the encoded scene and the current cognitive state of the individual.
The main takeaway from our work is that
eye movements are not just an epiphenomenon of mental imagery and memory, but rather that they play a central role in the retrieval process.
oculomotor behaviour is not just the by-product of mental imagery and memory but is actively and functionally involved in the retrieval process.
eye movements during memory retrieval are a reflection of mental imagery, and that the oculomotor system actively contributes to the retrieval of spatial information from episodic long term memory.
